items.headline: NEA issues daily haze alerts as transboundary smoke pushes central PSI past 100
items.summary: The NEA has published daily haze advisories since Sep 4 after the 24-hour PSI in central Singapore crossed 100 into the unhealthy band for the first time since 2023, driven by fires in southern Sumatra and Kalimantan; passing showers brought intermittent relief this week.

items.headline: Prosecutors seek up to 13.5 years' jail in fatal 2024 Tampines chain collision
items.summary: Prosecutors asked for up to 13.5 years' jail for a 45-year-old Singaporean who pleaded guilty over a 2024 Tampines chain collision that killed two, including a 17-year-old student; sentencing was adjourned.

items.headline: 52 Singaporeans detained in China over alleged pyramid-scheme links
items.summary: MFA said 52 Singaporeans were arrested and detained in Guangxi, China, over suspected pyramid-scheme activities; officers are in touch with families, and Second Minister Sim Ann said the Government is doing all it can to help.

items.headline: Update: Xi arrives for BRICS in first India trip since 2019, extending an olive branch to Modi
items.summary: Xi Jinping travelled to New Delhi for the 18th BRICS summit — his first India visit since before the 2020 Galwan clash — with a Modi–Xi bilateral expected to focus on the Himalayan border, trade and restoring links, marking a cautious thaw.

items.headline: Modi backs central-bank digital currencies to settle BRICS trade
items.summary: Chairing BRICS, Modi is promoting central-bank digital currencies and stronger cross-border payment links to settle more intra-bloc trade in local currencies, while stopping short of endorsing any move to replace the US dollar.

items.headline: BRICS finance chiefs, hosted by India, demand urgent IMF and World Bank reform
items.summary: BRICS finance ministers and central-bank governors meeting in New Delhi reiterated calls for urgent reform of the IMF and World Bank so they better reflect emerging economies; the expanded bloc now spans 11 members and about a quarter of world GDP.

items.headline: Modi says India's 7.8% growth 'gives confidence to the world' as BRICS opens
items.summary: Ahead of the summit Modi said India is growing at 7.8% and its 'reforms express' will continue, positioning the host as the bloc's fastest-growing major economy even as an oil-driven sell-off pressured the rupee.

items.headline: UK economy unexpectedly grows 0.4% in July as AI lifts services
items.summary: Official figures released Sep 11 showed UK GDP rose 0.4% in July, beating forecasts of no growth, with services — led by computer programming and AI-related work — driving the pickup, giving PM Burnham a rare economic boost.

items.headline: Burnham's signature devolution drive faces doubts over funding
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham's plan to shift power from Whitehall — giving England's mayors a share of income tax and creating a 'Number 10 North' — is his defining policy, but analysts warn it lacks clear funding answers and could falter.

items.headline: Update: Houthis complete their takeover of the Bab el-Mandeb strait, seizing Perim island
items.summary: Iran-aligned Houthis reached Perim (Mayyun) island after government forces withdrew, completing control of the strategic strait a day after seizing Mokha, threatening a key oil-shipping chokepoint and handing Iran fresh leverage.

items.headline: Israeli air strikes kill at least 12 in southern Lebanon as raids intensify
items.summary: Israeli air attacks killed at least 12 people, including children, in Kfar Reman in southern Lebanon amid an intensifying campaign that has left dozens dead in recent days despite a June framework truce; Israel cited Hezbollah drone launches.

items.headline: Putin lands in New Delhi for a BRICS summit shadowed by the Iran and Ukraine wars
items.summary: Putin arrived in India for the 18th BRICS summit, joining Xi Jinping and Iran's Pezeshkian as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine tested the bloc's push for greater clout, with leaders expected to press for local-currency trade.

items.headline: Expanded 11-member BRICS meets in Delhi, testing its challenge to a Western-led order
items.summary: The summit gathers the expanded bloc — now including Iran, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia and the UAE — amid debate over how far it can reshape global governance and finance; India has steered it toward pragmatic cooperation.

items.headline: OpenAI signals it may slow cutting-edge AI, Altman tells staff
items.summary: CEO Sam Altman told OpenAI employees the company is open to pacing its most advanced AI development and hopes rivals will follow, while acknowledging some may not agree, as executives touted an 'AGI era.'

items.headline: Microsoft plans to add 26 gigawatts of data-center capacity as compute runs short
items.summary: Microsoft mapped a buildout to more than 38 gigawatts of data-center capacity by 2032, roughly tripling today's ~12GW, after shortages forced it to turn away some AI and cloud business.

items.headline: OpenAI ends its $1-a-year US government deal, shifts to usage pricing at half off
items.summary: OpenAI is winding down the pilot that let federal agencies use its models for $1 a year, moving to usage-based pricing that gives government workers a 50% discount to standard rates.

items.headline: Silicon Valley leaders escalate warnings over AI's existential risks
items.summary: Warnings about catastrophic AI risk grew louder after a researcher quit and accused former employers OpenAI and Anthropic of 'racing toward super-intelligent AI'; Anthropic said it had blocked several attempts to misuse its models for bioweapons research.

items.headline: Nvidia's Huang says AI will transform the cybersecurity market
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said cybersecurity is the next big market for AI, predicting the technology will reshape how companies defend their systems and framing it as a major new source of demand for AI computing.

items.headline: US inflation holds at 3.4% in August, cementing Fed rate-hike bets
items.summary: August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% year-on-year, in line with forecasts, while core CPI ran a slightly hot 0.3% (2.4% annual); gasoline drove over a third of the gain, hardening expectations of a Fed hike on Sep 16.

items.headline: Update: Wall Street snaps a four-day slide as oil retreats
items.summary: US stocks rebounded Friday — the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq each up about 1% — as oil fell, breaking a four-session losing streak, though all three ended the week lower; markets put the odds of a 25bp Fed hike at roughly 85-90%.

items.headline: Oracle's contracted cloud backlog balloons to a record $664 billion
items.summary: Oracle said its remaining performance obligations jumped $209 billion year-on-year to a record $664 billion, with revenue up 30% to $19.3 billion and cloud-infrastructure sales up 121%; shares hit an all-time high.

items.headline: RH jumps on an earnings beat while Adobe slides despite raising its outlook
items.summary: RH rallied after Q2 revenue of $922 million beat estimates, while Adobe fell about 3% as soft Q4 guidance overshadowed a strong quarter and record recurring revenue; Kroger dropped about 3% on mixed results.

items.headline: Tencent-backed chipmaker Enflame nearly triples on its Shanghai debut
items.summary: Shares of Enflame, a Chinese AI-chip maker and Nvidia rival, soared roughly 200% on their Shanghai debut after a 6.12 billion yuan ($913 million) IPO valuing it near $25 billion; it is the last of China's 'four little dragons' of AI chips to list.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev reaches the US Open final, his third straight Grand Slam final
items.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev beat Karen Khachanov 6-3, 7-6, 7-6 to reach the US Open final and a third consecutive Grand Slam final, after his French Open title and Wimbledon runner-up finish; he awaits the Shelton–Tiafoe winner.

items.headline: 🎾 Sabalenka to meet Rybakina in the US Open women's final
items.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka beat Jessica Pegula in straight sets and Elena Rybakina ended Coco Gauff's run 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up Saturday's final; Sabalenka can be the first woman to win three straight US Open titles since Serena Williams (2012-14).

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell tops opening practice for the first Madrid Spanish Grand Prix
items.summary: George Russell set the pace in first practice for the inaugural Spanish GP at Madrid's new Madring circuit, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli fastest in FP2; qualifying is Saturday and the race Sunday.

items.headline: 🏏 Sri Lanka beat Pakistan to set up a Women's Asia Cup final against India
items.summary: Defending champions Sri Lanka chased 131 with two balls to spare, beating Pakistan by four wickets to reach the Women's T20 Asia Cup final against India in Dubai on Sep 12 — a repeat of the 2024 final Sri Lanka won.

items.headline: Hubble spots a giant 10-sided storm ringing Saturn's south pole
items.summary: Astronomers using Hubble identified a decagon — a ten-sided jet-stream wave about 104,000 miles across — encircling Saturn's south pole, a geometric twin to the famous northern hexagon and the first large regular-sided pattern seen at the southern pole.

items.headline: NASA and SpaceX delay Crew-13 after an oxidizer leak on Dragon
items.summary: NASA and SpaceX pushed back the Crew-13 launch to the ISS after finding an oxidizer leak in Dragon's propulsion system during prelaunch processing; the crew includes NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney.

items.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope begins its million-mile hunt for dark energy
items.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is on a three-month cruise to L2, where it will survey wide swaths of sky with Hubble-like sharpness over a field about 100 times wider to probe dark matter, dark energy and exoplanets.

fun_fact.headline: The Hundred Years War actually lasted 116 years
fun_fact.body: The Hundred Years' War between England and France was neither a single continuous war nor exactly a hundred years long. It ran for 116 years, from 1337 to 1453, in a series of on-and-off conflicts broken up by long truces. The name was coined by historians centuries later, not by the people who lived through it.

puzzle.title: The Broken Clock
puzzle.body: A clock runs fast, gaining 20 minutes every hour (so in one real hour it advances 80 minutes). It was set correctly at 12:00 noon. When the fast clock displays 6:00 PM, what is the actual, correct time?
puzzle.approach: Set up the ratio between the clock's speed and real time, then work backwards from what the clock shows.
puzzle.answer: 4:30 PM. The clock runs at 4/3 of real speed (80 clock-minutes per 60 real minutes). Showing 6:00 PM = 360 clock-minutes since noon, so real time elapsed = 360 x (60/80) = 270 minutes = 4h30m; true time is 4:30 PM.

word_puzzle.title: Boxed In
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed. Top: P L G; Right: R E H; Bottom: O M T; Left: B I Y. Chain words hopping between sides (never two letters from the same side in a row); each new word starts with the previous word's last letter; use all 12 letters in 2 words.
word_puzzle.approach: Chain two words covering all 12 letters, with each new word beginning on the previous word's last letter and no same-side letters in a row.
word_puzzle.answer: PROBLEM -> MIGHTY. PROBLEM (P-R-O-B-L-E-M) hops Top/Right/Bottom/Left/Top/Right/Bottom; MIGHTY begins on M and runs I-G-H-T-Y. Together the two words use all 12 letters exactly once.
